blocks.text: Splitting: When two contradictory states, such as love and hate, are compartmentalized and not integrated. Somebody is either all good, or all bad. Very extreme views of people, and it can switch quickly. Therapist will want to bring these two contradictions together: your friend did something hurtful, and there are things about them you really like. Are people allowed to make mistakes, and can we recover from that? Wanting to put these two extremes together.

blocks.text: Projection: Involves projecting undesirable feelings or emotions onto someone else, rather than admitting to or dealing with the unwanted feelings.

blocks.text: Projective Identification (specific to object relations): Refers to a psychological process in which a person will project a thought or belief that they have onto a second person. Then, in most common definitions of projective identification, there is another action in which the second person is changed by the projection and begins to behave as though they are, in fact, actually characterized by those thoughts or beliefs that have been projected. The client is projecting onto the therapist a feeling of annoyance. What happens is the therapist realizes they feel annoyed. The therapist takes on the feeling themselves, they begin to identify with the feeling, the therapist finds themselves feeling annoyed. That’s the unconscious manipulation of the client putting those feelings onto the therapist. Sexual attraction: Therapist would say it’s really the client having those unconscious feelings towards the therapist.

blocks.text: Identification occurs when a person not only takes on a belief or voice of another person, but also begins to identify with that individual. In this case, the husband has not merely taken on the idea that women should do the housework; rather, he sees himself as the head of his household, like his father. He is identifying with his father. Because of this identification, he expects to be treated like his father, with his wife respecting him and treating him as his mom treated his dad.
